architecture.mechanism: controlled discharge process using a boost converter and single-phase grid-tied inverter to transfer energy and heat the battery
architecture.intervention: Implement a parasitic load circuit mimicking the paper's boost converter topology to induce rapid deep-discharge and thermal stress on the R526 battery while parked, preventing recovery of surface charge.
architecture.expected_effect: The battery voltage remains below the cranking threshold after 24 hours due to complete energy depletion and increased internal resistance from thermal effects, contradicting the observed normal cranking.
architecture.falsification_test: Connect a programmable electronic load to the R526 battery simulating the identified leakage profile; if the battery recovers to crank normally after 24 hours of idle post-discharge, the mechanism is falsified.
